scope: Ordinary library UTF-8 scalar encoding, String reserve/push_scalar/scalar-count truncation/owned substring/is_empty, plus the complete existing impl236 library target replay.

identity.algorithm: SHA256 of sorted path + NUL + file SHA256 + LF
identity.paths: Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, tracked lib/**, crates/**/src/**, crate Cargo.toml/build.rs
identity.verification: Independently recomputed from exact Git blobs; all five selected source/test hashes matched. Std library text and ZIL fixtures are embedded in the retained harness.

retained_harness.binding: Copied before author target reuse and independently SHA-verified against the committed exact source receipt.

independent_execution.purpose: Supplemental exact runtime C-input binding; allocator probe hash independently matched exact Git both before and after this fault-injection replay.

source_review: encoded_len rejects negative, out-of-range and surrogate code points. encode validates scalar and output capacity before the first write, then emits standard shortest-form 1/2/3/4-byte UTF-8 using bounded arithmetic and checked u8 conversions.

Actual native loop visits every valid Unicode scalar from0 through0x10FFFF excluding surrogates and decodes the emitted bytes back to the same scalar and exact width. Invalid and too-short cases preserve sentinel output; the emoji byte sequence also has an independent exact-byte oracle.

push_scalar encodes into a local four-byte array then delegates to the existing ordinary append/replace implementation; invalid scalar returns before mutation. reserve validates requested bounds before the existing fallible ByteBuffer primitive.

truncate locates a scalar boundary before changing the buffer length. substring locates and bounds the source byte interval, then constructs a new owned validated String through from_utf8. The new String survives truncation and clear of its source.

No privileged String opcode or compiler capability is introduced. Private owning ByteBuffer and existing resource-head borrowing proofs remain the representation; all new operations are ordinary ZIL source.

Complete target replay retains actual import/source-identity and private-helper rejection, source-byte budget/cache controls, iterator order/alias negatives, Store owner transfers and allocation-failure state preservation, and the original three component lifecycle tests.

native_evidence.result: exit0 with empty stdout/stderr and no fallback in all four; actual complete valid-scalar loop per executable
native_evidence.failure_controls: Invalid scalar, zero byte limit and invalid scalar truncation propagate errors without executing the success continuation and preserve length/capacity. Sentinel output and owned-substring independence are actual runtime observations.

limitations: New Unicode operations do not provide Unicode normalization, grapheme segmentation or locale processing.
substring returns a new owner; arbitrary borrowed/lending substrings are not claimed.

The new Unicode fixture has invalid-input/capacity controls, not new allocator fault injection for each added String wrapper. Existing Store allocation failures were independently replayed; previous String allocator checks retain their prior exact-candidate identity.
Author Clippy not independently rerun; this is no full-workspace, native-Windows, Rust comparison, complete standard-library or full-language acceptance.
